title: occupancy and latency across a100 h100 l40s
content:
Summary:
This note captures a focused investigation into how GPU occupancy, cloud SKU choice, and driver/CUDA versions affect latency variance and cost-efficiency for our serving runtime. We compared A100, H100, and L40S across representative cloud SKUs (AWS, GCP, Azure) and across three driver/CUDA stack permutations. The goal: identify predictable SLO-safe hardware+driver combos and surface any pathological occupancy regimes that cause latency tail-jitter or throughput cliffs.

Motivation / Context:
- Recent customer reports of 99th percentile latency spikes when moving from p4d -> p5d (A100->H100) despite nominally higher FLOPS.
- We need deterministic guidance for Dedicated capacity sizing and autoscaler thresholds, and to decide whether to mark some driver versions as unsupported for production.

Test matrix (high level):
- Models: GPT-small-ish 1.3B decoder (attention heavy), 7B quantized INT8 (+4-bit experiment), and a 70B-like encoder-decoder microbenchmark (reduced batch tokens to fit memory).
- Precision modes: FP16, TF32 (where applicable), and INT8 quantized kernels for the 7B tests.
- SKUs: AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100 40GB), AWS p5.24xlarge (H100 80GB), GCP a2-megagpu (A100 variant), Azure ND96asr v4 (A100), Azure HBv4-like H100 preview, Azure L40S NVv5-equivalent. We label them A100, H100, L40S for readability.
- Driver/CUDA stacks: (A) Driver 470 / CUDA 11.8, (B) Driver 525 / CUDA 12.1, (C) Driver 535 / CUDA 12.2 (latest during test).
- Occupancy sweeps: single-request latencies, batch sizes from 1 up to 32 tokens per request, concurrent inflight requests from 1 to 48 (to map occupancy and KV-cache memory pressure).
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, achieved occupancy (CUDA SM occupancy), peak memory, and kernel-time breakdown (cuBLAS/cuDNN/cudaMemcpy/other).

Methodology notes:
- Each cell (model x SKU x stack x precision x concurrency) was run for 10 warmup iterations then 300 measured iterations. We used our internal stress harness (bench/serving-load-gen v2) pinned to a single CPU core per client thread to avoid host scheduling variance.
- Clock frequency governors set to "performance" where the cloud provider allowed. We recorded GPU clocks and NVLink traffic where supported.
- For INT8 we used our quantized runtime with operator fusion enabled; we toggled fusion to capture regression cases.
- Profiling: lightweight CUPTI sampling at 1% (low noise) + one full Nsight Systems trace per interesting cell.

Key findings (high level):
1) H100 gives higher overall tokens/sec but significantly more p99 jitter in CUDA 12.2 on our fused kernels.
   - Observed ~1.3x throughput vs A100 for FP16 small models at high concurrency (24+ inflight).
   - However p99 latency increased by ~30-60% vs A100 under the same concurrency in stack C (Driver 535/CUDA 12.2).
   - Cause trace: kernel selection falls back to a new auto-tuned matmul kernel that stair-steps performance at certain sequence lengths; combined with heavier register pressure causes occasional long-running kernels (seen in Nsight samples).

2) L40S shows excellent INT8 quantized throughput and lower median latency for 7B INT8 workloads, but memory fragmentation under high occupancy leads to sudden OOM or high memcpy churn for large token contexts.
   - In INT8 7B runs, L40S achieved ~1.6x tokens/sec vs A100 with our INT8 backend.
   - At concurrency >32 with long contexts (>1024 tokens), we observed repeated CUDA memcpy spikes and p99 outliers; telemetry shows small free-block fragmentation in driver allocator.

3) A100 remains the most stable baseline across driver stacks, particularly on Driver 525/CUDA 12.1 (stack B).
   - p99 tails were lowest and CPU->GPU memcpy overhead predictable.
   - For FP16 workloads A100 gave near-linear scaling up to 16 concurrent requests, after which batching and KV cache eviction policy needed re-tuning.

4) Driver/CUDA interactions matter more than raw hardware for tail behavior.
   - Stack C (535/12.2) enabled some new kernels that improve steady-state throughput but introduced bimodal latency distributions.
   - Stack A (470/11.8) shows lower peak throughput but very consistent latencies and fewer memory fragmentation artifacts.

Representative numbers (single-run examples, approximate):
- 1.3B FP16 model, batch=1, concurrency=8:
  - A100 (stack B): p50=22ms, p95=38ms, p99=55ms, tokens/sec=18k
  - H100 (stack C): p50=16ms, p95=42ms, p99=83ms, tokens/sec=24k
  - L40S (stack B): p50=19ms, p95=40ms, p99=62ms, tokens/sec=20k
- 7B INT8, batch=2, concurrency=24:
  - A100 (stack B): p50=85ms, p95=160ms, p99=230ms, tokens/sec=6.8k
  - H100 (stack B): p50=72ms, p95=158ms, p99=210ms, tokens/sec=8.9k
  - L40S (stack B): p50=52ms, p95=110ms, p99=290ms (fragmentation spikes), tokens/sec=11k

Profiling observations (kernel-level):
- cuBLAS matmul kernels dominate for FP16; NVFuser-generated fused kernels dominate for transformer ffn/attn in some stacks.
- On H100 with stack C, we saw a new matmul kernel that uses more SMs but with longer latency variance per kernel call — the result is better throughput but higher tail.
- memcpy hotspots on L40S correlate with driver allocator metadata locks when free list becomes fragmented (observed in Nsight thread traces).

Operational implications:
- For strict 99th SLOs (e.g., <150ms for interactive features), prefer A100 with stack B or stack A. H100 can be used but requires conservative autoscaler thresholds and larger warmup pools to amortize kernel selection variability.
- For pure throughput/cost-optimization on high-volume batched workloads (e.g., embedding bulk jobs or async pipelines), L40S with INT8 is attractive but should be isolated to dedicated pools with shorter max context sizes to avoid fragmentation issues.
- Pin driver stacks for Dedicated reservations. Avoid automatic upgrade to driver 535 / CUDA 12.2 on H100 until we complete mitigations for the tail behavior.

Mitigations we tested (and results):
- Kernel pinning: forcing older matmul kernels removed the p99 bimodality at a ~6% throughput cost on H100. Good temporary mitigation.
- Fragmentation workaround: pre-allocate a slab arena for KV caches reduced memcpy spikes on L40S in 80% of trials.
- Fusion toggle: disabling a specific NVFuser fusion pattern reduced tail in stack C but incurred 10-12% latency increase for p50.

Recommendations (short):
- Default Dedicated image: A100 with Driver 525 / CUDA 12.1 for general-purpose low-tail inference. Mark as "recommended default" in Capacity docs.
- H100: allowed for high-throughput customers but behind a feature flag; require autoscaler margin + prewarm pools; do not auto-upgrade drivers beyond 525 until follow-up work.
- L40S: target for INT8-heavy workloads and batch jobs only. Add pre-allocation slab for KV cache and hard limit max context for pools using L40S.
- Add CI matrix entry that runs a 2-hour p99 stability run on all stacks weekly (SRV-847).

Next steps / action items:
- (Evan) Create a short follow-up perf PR to implement kernel pinning toggle and expose it via runtime config (GH PR linked).
- (Priya) Add L40S slab allocator prototype to our private runtime branch and smoke test with long-context 7B quant runs.
- (Diego) Run full nightly sweep with longer traces (Nsight) for H100 stack C to capture rare long-tail kernels and open bugs with vendor.
- (Asha) Draft Dedicated capacity guidance doc and update Console SKU recommendation page.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are we confident the fragmentation on L40S is purely driver allocator behavior or is our custom KV cache interaction aggravating it? Needs allocator-level trace with driver vendor.
- Can NV vendor provide a pinned kernel selection option for H100 to avoid the new auto-tuner for specific sequence-length buckets?

Appendix (short):
- Repro commands: bench/serving-load-gen --model gpt-small-v1 --precision fp16 --concurrency 24 --backend dedicated --driver 525 --trace nsight-sample
- Raw data location: s3://redwood-telemetry/benchmarks/2025-11/occupancy-sweep/{sku}/{stack}/{model}/metrics.csv
- Full Nsight traces: gs://redwood-traces/serving-runtime/2025-11-20/

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an in-progress doc; numbers are representative samples. We intentionally kept the 70B-like run small to focus on kernel behavior. Please comment with additional cells you'd like to see in the matrix (e.g., more CUDA versions, other quant backends).
